options.text: Liquid X has stronger intermolecular forces than liquid Y: its higher boiling point shows that the covalent bonds inside its molecules are stronger.
options.why: Confuses intermolecular forces with the covalent bonds inside molecules.

options.text: Liquid X has stronger intermolecular forces than liquid Y: its lower vapor pressure and higher boiling point show that fewer of its particles can overcome the attractions between particles and escape into the gas phase.
options.why: A lower vapor pressure and a higher boiling point both reflect stronger attractions between particles.

options.text: Liquid X has weaker intermolecular forces than liquid Y: its lower vapor pressure shows that its particles escape from the liquid more easily at a given temperature.
options.why: Reverses the link between vapor pressure and the strength of attractions.

options.why: Claims the particles of X move faster, although both liquids are at the same temperature.
